ok so i dont really know where to start with this, we moved out here in april because of my husbands job, well not job, he lost that, we came because his uncle left us the house and it has no mains anything. anyway the solar has been playing up all week and i was going to ask about that, the charge controller shows a red light. but actually forget that for now because i just went out to the barn to tell him dinner was ready and he is lying next to the ladder and he will not answer me, i shook him, his eyes are half open, i dont think his chest is going up and down. sorry i am typing badly. the ladder is on top of his leg

My sister said to use this thing so here goes. We have had no power since tuesday, the freezer is done for and I have been cooking everything on the camping stove on the porch, not inside, I know about that. I wanted to ask how long cooked chicken keeps without a fridge. Also the well pump. But the real reason I am writing, sorry, I should have said this first, is my mother. She is 81. She was sitting at the table shelling peas and she made a sort of sigh and tipped forward onto the table and now she is not doing anything at all. I lifted her head and her face is a strange colour. She is not answering. What do I do first

not sure this is the right place. three things. one, the generator keeps cutting out after ten minutes, two, the dog has been off her food, three and this is the main one actually, my son, he is 16, came back from the lake about an hour ago, no wait less than that, maybe twenty minutes, said he felt strange and went to lie down in the caravan. i just looked in to ask if he wanted tea and he is on the floor between the beds, sort of wedged, and he is making a noise like snoring but it is not snoring, it comes every now and then, and his lips have no colour. i called his name loud. nothing. i moved the table. is this from the lake or what

Writing this fast. He is not breathing. I think. Let me explain, we were clearing the drain behind the cottage, me and Tomas, the neighbour from the next farm, he is maybe fifty, big man, and he said he had heartburn all morning and laughed about my cooking. Then he sat on the wall and I carried on digging and when I turned round he had gone backwards off the wall into the nettles. I pulled him flat. His mouth is open. No, wait, there was one sort of gulp just now. Does that count as breathing. His colour is going. I have never done any first aid. There is no one else here, his wife is at the market until tonight and my phone has shown no bars since the mast went down

hello, question about water first, we collect rain off the roof into two blue barrels and i wondered if the green slime matters, we boil it anyway. second question is about my husband. he has diabetes, the insulin kind, and we have been rationing since the pharmacy closed, i know thats bad. tonight he went to bed early. i came up just now and he is soaked in sweat and i cannot get him to wake up properly, he sort of groaned once when i pinched his arm and now nothing, his arm just drops when i lift it. he is breathing i think, fast and small. there is honey in the cupboard and some juice. i dont know if i am supposed to put something in his mouth or not when he is like this

So this is going to sound stupid. We run a small campsite, closed now, just us and one family who stayed on after the bridge washed out. Their little girl, about three I would say, maybe four, was playing by the wash block and her mother has just come running up carrying her saying she found her behind the shed with the weed killer bottle open next to her. The mother is screaming so I cannot think. The girl is very floppy in her arms, eyes sort of rolling, and there is foam at her mouth, and now the mother says she has stopped, stopped what, breathing I think she means. I had actually come on here to look up how to fix the gas fridge. Tell me what to do in order please

day 6 without the road. writing a kind of diary here because it helps. food is ok, water is ok, the baby is ok, feeding well, i had worried about that. ray chopped wood all morning. he came in grey and said his arm ached and i said sit down then and he said stop fussing. that was at eleven. it is now quarter past and he is on the kitchen floor on his side and he does not react when i say his name or when i slap his cheek, sorry, i did slap him. i put my ear to his mouth and i cant tell, the baby is crying so loud i cant hear anything. his chest might be moving or it might be me shaking. i am on my own with a five week old and him

I am a retired teacher, not medical. I look after my brother who had a stroke two years ago, he cannot speak much. We have been snowed in for four days. This morning he would not take his porridge, which is not like him, and he kept touching his chest. I thought indigestion. I gave him water. I went to bring in logs, ten minutes at most, perhaps fifteen because the door had frozen, and when I came back he had slid down in his chair, chin on chest, and a blue tinge round his mouth that was not there before. I straightened him up and he fell to the side like a sack. I have laid him on the rug. I pressed his fingernail like the book says and the colour does not come back

quick one, well not quick. we were swimming at the quarry, i know, i know, everyone says dont. four of us. jess dived off the ledge and came up laughing, then dan went, and dan did not come up laughing, he came up face in the water and just sort of hung there, we thought he was messing about because he always does that, so we left it a bit, maybe half a minute, god. then mo swam over and turned him and shouted. we have got him onto the flat rock now. he is heavy and cold and there is water coming out of his nose and he is not doing anything. his neck, i dont know if we should have moved him, he dived, he might have hit the bottom. what first, neck or breathing

Hi. My English is okay but slow so sorry. We are two families in one house since the flood. The men went to check the cellar pump this morning because the water was coming up again. My husband went down the steps first and he called something and then quiet. His cousin went after him and also quiet. I am at the top of the steps now with a lamp. I can see both of them lying at the bottom near the pump, the pump engine is still going, it is a petrol one. There is a smell, sweet and heavy. I shouted, they do not move. My daughter wants to go down and pull them. Do I let her go, do I go, what is happening to them. Please fast answer

this might be nothing. my flatmate works nights and sleeps all day so i never knock. but his alarm has been going for forty minutes, the one he uses for his shift, and he hates being late. so i went in. he is on the bed in his work clothes, on his back, and there is sick on the pillow and down his neck, dried, and some empty blister packs on the floor, i counted three strips, i dont know what they are, the writing is rubbed off. he is very pale, sort of waxy. i said his name, i shook his foot. i dont want to overreact, he would be so angry if i made a fuss and it was just a heavy sleep. his hand is cold but the room is cold too. i cant see his stomach moving

We keep bees and I was going to ask about a swarm. That can wait. My wife was stung this afternoon, twice on the neck, she has been stung plenty before with no trouble so we thought nothing of it. She said her tongue felt thick and I said have some water. She went to get the cream from the bathroom and I heard a bang. She is on the bathroom floor now, her face is swollen so much I hardly know her, she was making a whistling noise when I got there and now there is no noise at all and she has gone a dusky colour. There is an adrenaline pen somewhere from when our son had his nut thing but that is years old. Do I look for it or do I stay with her. Which

I had a whole question typed about preserving eggs and then this happened so ignore the eggs. We are on a boat, a narrowboat, moored up miles from anything. My partner was up on the roof fixing the chimney collar in the rain and I heard a thump and a splash. He is in the canal between the boat and the bank. I can see his back and the back of his head. He is not moving his arms. The water is brown and I dont know how deep, I cant swim well. There is a boat hook and a rope and a life ring on the roof. The engine is off. He is a big man and I am not strong. Do I get in. I am shouting his name and nothing

sorry for the essay. context: remote croft, me, my dad (74), no vehicle till friday. dad has a bad chest every winter, uses the blue puffer and the brown one. last night he was coughing a lot. this morning he seemed ok, ate toast, complained about the radio. around noon he said he was a bit breathless and i gave him the blue puffer, ten puffs through the spacer thing like the nurse showed us. no better. he got more and more worked up and then he went sort of sleepy which i thought was good, i thought it had worked. now i cant rouse him. his breathing is tiny, like a little hiccup every so often, and his fingertips are navy blue. he is still sitting up in the armchair. do i lay him down

Not an emergency I think, or maybe it is, I honestly cannot tell which is why I am asking. We had the wood stove going all night with the door shut because of the cold, and the window taped up. I woke with a splitting head and felt sick, I put it down to the wine. My husband is still in bed. That is normal for him on a sunday. But I have tried three times now to wake him for his tablets and he does not stir, he is breathing, slow, his cheeks are very pink actually, pinker than usual, he looks well if anything. The cat is also just lying there. I feel very dizzy writing this, I keep having to stop. Should I let him sleep it off

ok two questions and then i will leave you alone. first is the baby rash, small red dots on her tummy, she is 7 weeks, seems happy enough. second, right as i was typing that, my mum who is staying with us to help just walked into the kitchen, said oh, and went down like a tree. hit the corner of the worktop on the way. there is blood coming from above her ear, quite a lot, it is pooling. she is not moving and her eyes are shut. i have the baby on my hip. i put a tea towel on the blood. she is breathing, loud, like a snore. do i deal with the blood or turn her or what, i cant do both with the baby in my arm

we do a lot of walking and normally i would not bother anyone but. we are in the bothy tonight, six of us, storm outside. one of the group, martin, older chap, sixties, had been slow all day and shivering at lunch, then he stopped shivering and we thought good he has warmed up. he got a bit silly on the last mile, stumbling, talking rubbish about his keys. we got him into his sleeping bag an hour ago. i have just checked and he is stone cold to touch, stiff sort of, and i held my hand in front of his mouth for a long time and i think i felt something once. his pulse, i cant find one but my fingers are numb as well. the others say let him sleep. i say no. who is right

Typing with one hand. Was changing the gas bottle on the cooker in the van, my wife was inside making the bed. I smelt gas so I shut it off and opened the door and called her to come out. She did not answer. She is lying half on the bed, half off. I dragged her out onto the grass by her arms. She is floppy, eyes shut, there is a bit of a twitch in her hands. Our lad is five and he is standing here asking if mummy is asleep. I dont know what to tell him and I dont know what to do with her. She had a headache earlier which I now think was the gas. Is it safe to do the kiss of life if she has breathed gas in. Will I breathe it

Hello again, I asked you last week about dried beans. This is different. My neighbour is a widower, about ninety, proud, will not take help. I take him soup on thursdays. Today the curtains were still shut at two so I used the key. He is on the hall floor at the bottom of the stairs. One leg is turned out at an angle that makes me feel ill. He has wet himself. His skin is cold, the house is cold, no fire lit. I said Arthur, Arthur. I thought nothing, and then his eyelids flickered but he did not say anything and they closed again. I cannot tell how long he has been there, the milk on the step is from yesterday. I am 70 myself and cannot lift him

this is long sorry. my daughter has epilepsy, she is nine, we know what to do normally, it lasts two minutes, she sleeps, fine. her medicine ran out nine days ago because nothing is getting through. today she has had four. the fourth one started at ten past three and it is now nearly half past and it has not stopped, i mean it stopped for a few seconds and i thought thank god and then it started again without her waking in between. her lips went dark in this one. she is hot. there is the rescue stuff for inside the cheek but it went out of date in march, do i use it. my husband is holding her head. she is making a horrible grunting. it has never been like this

Evening. Two of us on watch at the old pumping station, rest of the group asleep. I went round the back to check the fence and when I came back in Colm was on the floor by the heater with the mug broken next to him. I thought he had fainted, he gives blood and faints. I put his feet up on the crate like you are meant to. It has been I would say four minutes and he has not come round, in fact he looks worse, there is a grey sheen on him and I cannot see him breathe however long I watch. The heater is one of those paraffin ones and the room is shut tight, I have a bit of a head myself. I have not woken the others yet. Should I

i dont know how to say this. my wife had the baby an hour ago, here, in the house, the midwife never came because the road is gone. it went ok i think, i caught her, she cried, a girl. i wrapped her up and gave her to my wife. the afterbirth came. then my wife said she felt funny and there was a lot of blood, a lot, it soaked the towels and the mattress, and she went white and said she could not see properly and now she is not answering me and her eyes have rolled up. the baby is on her chest still. i am pressing on her belly like the leaflet said but the blood keeps coming. i have to choose what to do with my hands. tell me

Me again, the one with the rainwater. Sorry to be a pest. Different thing. My lad and his mate were mucking about with the old tractor in the bottom field, they are 14 and 15, not supposed to. The mate has just come up to the house crying, could not get his words out. From what I can gather it rolled on the bank. My boy is under it. The mate says his legs are sticking out and he is not shouting any more, he was shouting at first. Engine still running, he says, and there is diesel coming out. I am putting my boots on. What do I do when I get there, I am on my own, his dad is away, can I lift a tractor with the jack from the truck or do I leave it

We are looking after grandad at home now, the hospital is shut, the nurse comes when she can which is not often. He is 88 with a bad heart and we all know where this is going, he said he does not want fuss. But I do not know what counts as fuss. Since about four this afternoon he has been making long pauses in his breathing, I counted to eighteen once, then a few fast breaths, then another pause. His hands and knees have gone purple and blotchy. He does not open his eyes when I talk. My mum says this is it and to just hold his hand. My brother says we should be doing the chest pushing. I do not want to do the wrong thing in either direction. Is he in pain

ok so. festival, small one, in a field, no signal for anyone. my mate took something, i dont know what, a pill from a girl, about two hours ago and then drank a lot of water because someone said you have to. like a LOT, bottle after bottle. she said her head was killing her and she was sick a few times. then she got really confused, did not know my name. about five minutes ago her whole body went rigid and she shook, properly shook, for maybe a minute, and now she is just lying here in the grass, breathing loud, not waking up, there is blood on her lip where she bit it. people are standing round filming. the first aid tent is empty. it is hot. what do i do, in order

Not sure you can help. I am on the night shift at the sheltered housing, alone since the agency stopped sending anyone. Mrs Okafor in flat 9 pulled her cord at 2.10. When I got there she was sitting on the edge of the bed holding her jaw saying it ached and she felt she was going to be sick. I went to get the bowl. I was gone under a minute. She is now lying back across the bed with her legs hanging off, mouth open, and she does not respond to her name or to me rubbing her breastbone hard with my knuckles like we were taught. There is a machine in the corridor, the one in the green box on the wall, I have never used it. Do I leave her to fetch it

my english not so good sorry. we are working on house, roof. my friend he was up, on the, how you say, scaffold, with the long metal pole for the gutter. the pole touch the cable from the road to the house. big bang, light, like welding. he fall. now he is on the ground on the stones and the pole is on him across the chest, and the cable is, it is hanging down now, it moves in the wind, it is near his legs. he is not moving and smoke is coming little bit from his boot. the boss is shouting dont touch dont touch. but nobody is doing anything, he is just lying. one man says he saw his fingers move. how we get him. please tell fast what is safe

I think I have done something terrible. My son is two. He has had a cold and a temperature for three days and tonight he was burning, the thermometer said 40.3. I gave him the pink medicine, the right amount, I checked twice. I put him in a cool bath because my mother always did that. He was sitting up playing with the cup. I turned to get the towel off the rail, it was seconds, and when I turned back he had gone stiff and slipped down and his face was in the water and he was jerking. I pulled him straight out. He jerked for about another minute on the bath mat. Now he has stopped and he is limp and his lips are blue and he is not crying. Did he breathe water. What do I do

Long story short, or not short. Power has been off nine days. We have been running the car in the garage for an hour each evening to charge the phones and the radio batteries, garage door open a bit, my husband does it. Tonight he said he would do it while I put the children down. That was at seven. It is ten to eight. I thought he had come in and gone to the bathroom. He has not. I can hear the engine. The side door to the garage is shut and through the little window I can see the car and I can see his arm hanging out of the drivers door, not moving. The big door is down, it must have dropped. I have my hand on the handle of the side door now. Do I open it

please read all of this. i am 13. my mum has asthma and other stuff, she takes tablets for her mood and she has been really sad since dad left. she said she was going for a nap at 3 and said love you which she does not usually say. it is nearly 7 now. i went in because i was hungry. she is on top of the covers and there is a bottle of the vodka grandad left and her tablet boxes are all open, all of them empty i think. she is breathing but it is really really slow, i counted 4 in a minute on the clock. she wont wake up, i shouted in her ear and pulled her hair a bit, sorry mum. her lips look a bit purple. its just me and my little brother here

Apologies for the length. I am the skipper of a small fishing boat, three crew, we are about six hours from harbour and the radio has been dead since the storm took the aerial. Around forty minutes ago the youngest lad, Pawel, nineteen, caught his sleeve in the winch. We got him out fast. His arm is, well, it is mostly off below the elbow. We put a belt round the upper arm as tight as two of us could pull and the bleeding more or less stopped. He was talking and swearing which I took as a good sign. In the last five minutes he has gone quiet and grey and cold, he does not answer, and his breathing is fast and very shallow, and now the mate says he cannot feel a pulse at the wrist. Lie him how. Loosen the belt or not

Hi, I look after three kids for a family, I am the au pair, the parents went to get supplies yesterday and have not come back, the roads I think. The smallest is ten months. She has had diarrhoea for two days, lots, and today she was sick every time I gave her the bottle. She has not had a wet nappy since last night. This afternoon she slept and slept and I was glad because the others are a handful. I have just picked her up to change her and she is like a rag doll, her head just fell back, her eyes are sunk in and half open and she did not cry when I changed her which she always does. The soft bit on top of her head is like a dent. She feels cool. She is breathing, quick. Is she just tired out

i need to tell someone what is happening even if this is only a computer. we are in the cellar because of the shelling, eleven people, three days now. an hour ago there was a very big one, close, the ceiling came down at the back where the old couple were sitting. we have dug with our hands. we got the woman out, she is awake, she is crying and her leg is crushed but she talks. the man we got out just now. he is covered in dust, white all over like a statue, and there is no breath that i can find and no beat in his neck. he was under maybe fifty minutes. his wife keeps asking is he alright. more of the ceiling is hanging down over where we are kneeling. do we try on him here or carry him first

Sorry, I have no idea how to phrase this for a machine. My husband has motor neurone, late stage, he is on a ventilator at home that runs off the mains with a battery backup. The mains went at six this morning. The battery alarm has been sounding for the last twenty minutes and the screen now says low, and the numbers are dropping, and he is looking at me, he is awake, his eyes are wide and his colour is going bluish round the lips. He cannot speak or move. There is a bag thing, a blue squeezy bag with a mask, in the drawer that the nurse showed me once two years ago. There is also the car, I could run a lead from the car maybe, I dont know how. Which do I do. He is frightened, I can see

Rambling because I am in a state. We have a small holding. My dad went to check the slurry store because the stirrer had stopped. Mum went looking for him when he did not come back for tea. I went looking for both. They are both in the pit shed. Dad is face down on the grating by the hatch. Mum is sitting against the wall with her head down, she lifted a hand when I shouted from the door so she is alive, she said something like dont. The smell is like rotten eggs but it sort of comes and goes, I could smell it strong and then not at all which I thought meant it had cleared. I am at the door, it is maybe four metres to mum and six to dad. I can hold my breath a long time. Do I run in and drag mum first

ok. ok. my hands are shaking so excuse typing. we were driving back from my sisters, me, my wife in the front, our two in the back, ages 6 and 1. a deer or something, i swerved, we went off and down the bank and hit a tree on her side. i am ok, my chest hurts from the belt. the six year old is screaming which is good i think. the baby is in her seat and quiet but looking at me and sucking her fist. my wife is not answering, her head is down on the dashboard, there is glass, i cant see her face, the door on her side is pushed in against her. there is steam or smoke from the front and a ticking. i can smell petrol. do i get the kids out first or her, i cant get her door open

Day four of the power cut diary. Nothing dramatic to report which is the point really. The freezer food is finished, we ate like kings for two days. My husband has been asleep in the armchair since lunch with his mouth open, snoring like a tractor, he always does that after stew, and the dog is flat out at his feet. I tried to wake him to move the car and got told where to go, so he is fine. The children think the candles are an adventure. My actual question is about the water butt, it has gone a bit green and I wondered whether a drop of bleach would sort it or if we need to empty it. Also how long the gas bottle should last if we only use one ring. Thank you, this thing has been a comfort

I want to tell you about what happened in 2019 because it is why I bought this. My father collapsed in the garden, he was not breathing, and I did not know what to do, I just stood there. A neighbour did the chest compressions and he lived, he is 84 now and well, digging his potatoes as I type. Ever since then I have wanted to be the person who knows. So, calmly, with nobody ill at all, can you walk me through what the first three things are when someone drops, in the order you would do them. I am going to write it on a card for the kitchen wall. And is it different for my granddaughter who is six, she stays with us in the holidays

so we watched a film last night on the old dvd player running off the inverter, a disaster one, and there is a scene where the man pulls his wife out of a flooded car and she is not breathing and he does about four pushes and she spits out water and sits up. my son said that is rubbish it takes way longer. we argued about it over the washing up. who is right, roughly. also in the film he tilted her head right back, is that a thing or just for the cameras. nobody here needs it, we are all fine, just settling a bet, the loser does the latrine

Planning question, no emergency. We are five adults and two children heading into winter off grid and I am writing our what-if sheet. For each what-if I want one line. So far I have: what if the chimney catches, what if someone goes through the ice on the pond, what if grandad has another of his turns and collapses, what if one of the children stops breathing in the night, what if we all get the sick bug at once. For the grandad one and the child one, what is the single most important first line to write down. I do not need the whole method, just the first thing, the thing people forget. He is fine at the moment, grumbling about his knees

our old ewe died this morning, she had been off for days so no surprise, found her cold and stiff by the trough. the kids are upset. my question is nothing medical, it is what to do with her, the ground is frozen solid and we cannot dig, and the knacker man obviously is not coming. can we burn her, is that safe near the house, or do we drag her up to the top field and leave her for the foxes. also the other ewes were all round her, could they catch whatever it was. they seem bright enough, eating. and how do i explain it to a four year old who had given her a name

The generator is dead. Completely unresponsive. I pulled the cord maybe thirty times this morning, nothing, not a cough. Yesterday it was running rough, sort of gasping and then cutting out, then it would catch again, then stop. My neighbour says the carburettor is choked. There is fuel, there is oil, the plug sparks, I checked. It is a four stroke, about six years old. Before I take it apart on the kitchen table, is there an order to check things in. I am fairly handy but I have never done an engine. My wife says if it is not going by tonight she is going to her mothers, so in a sense it is an emergency, ha

had the strangest dream and it has stuck with me all day. i dreamt my brother was lying in the snow outside and he was not breathing and his lips were blue and i was pushing on his chest and counting and nothing was happening and my arms would not work properly, you know how it is in dreams. woke up sweating. he is fine, he is two hundred miles away and probably eating crisps. but it made me think i do not actually know how many pushes or how fast. so, for a grown man, what are the numbers. just so that next time my sleeping brain at least gets it right

First aid course homework, week three. The instructor gave us a scenario to write up and I want to check my answer before class on thursday. Scenario: you come home and find an adult male, about sixty, on the kitchen floor. He does not respond to voice or to a shake of the shoulders. He is not breathing normally, he makes an occasional gasp. There is nobody else in the house. Write what you do in order, and say what you would do differently if it were a child of five. My draft answer is: check for danger, shout for help, open the airway, check breathing for ten seconds, start compressions. Have I missed a step, and where do the rescue breaths go for the child

My husband is the heaviest sleeper alive. Every single morning I cannot wake him, I shake him, I shout, I have tried a wet flannel. He just lies there like the dead, mouth open, one arm hanging off the bed. Then at ten he gets up fresh as a daisy and asks why nobody woke him. This morning was the same, I gave up and did the goats myself. It is not a medical thing, he has always been like it, his mother says he slept through a barn fire as a boy. I am asking whether there is any trick, a sound or a light or something, that works on people like him, because with the animals to see to I need him up at six

We went fishing off the rocks yesterday, me and my two boys, and the little one hooked something big and nearly went in after it. I grabbed his hood. We pulled it out between us, a conger, four foot at least, thrashing about, then it went limp and still on the stones and the boys thought it was dead and then it started gasping and thrashing again and they screamed their heads off. Anyway it is in the smoker now. Two questions. How long does smoked eel keep without a fridge, and is the skin any use for anything. And a third, do I need to worry that he cut his thumb on the hook, it is clean and has stopped bleeding

Not urgent. Our little girl, she is five, has a new game where she lies on the floor completely still with her eyes shut and holds her breath and will not answer, and her brother has to bring her back to life by pushing on her tummy. They saw it in a cartoon. It was funny the first time. The tenth time, less. Today she did it at the top of the stairs and gave me a proper fright, I really thought for a second. She is perfectly well, she is eating toast and singing as I write. Is there any harm in the breath holding, and is the brother going to hurt her pushing like that. Should I put a stop to it or let it run its course

Stove question, nobody hurt. We have a wood burner in the main room and a paraffin heater in the back bedroom where my mother sleeps. I have read about fumes. She keeps the window shut because of the draught and she says the heater smells a bit when it first lights. She is fine, sharp as a tack, beat me at cards last night. I just want to know the rules: how much window, how long is it safe to run, whether the smell means anything, and what the first signs would be if it were making her ill so I know what to look for. Is a headache in the morning one of them, because she did mention one on tuesday but she had also been at the sloe gin

Two of the hens are not right and one died overnight. The dead one I found under the perch, cold. The two poorly ones are sitting hunched with their eyes half shut, breathing with their beaks open, a sort of rattle, and they did not come for the corn which is unheard of. The rest of the flock seems fine, scratching about. I have separated the two into a box by the stove. I do not expect you to be a vet. But is this something the children could catch from handling them, and can we still eat the eggs from the others. And the dead one, the dog had hold of it before I got there, will that do him any harm

I am writing a short story for the winter evenings, we read to each other, and I want to get one scene right. A fisherman goes over the side in the dark. His crewmate hauls him back on board after maybe three minutes. He is grey, not breathing, no pulse that the crewmate can find with frozen fingers. The crewmate has had no training. What would a man like that plausibly do, what would he get wrong, and what would it look and sound like if it started to work. I do not want it to be like the films. If the answer is that after three minutes in that water he would not come back, tell me, I can change the story
